claim: Deficiency of the transcription factor Srf (Srf −/−) causes embryonic lethality due to severe gastrulation defects.
source: As previously described, deficiency of the transcription factor Srf (Srf −/−) causes embryonic lethality due to severe gastrulation defects (Arsenian et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citation to Arsenian et al., 1998

claim: Offspring with the Srf fl/fl; Atoh1Cre genotype (Srf cKO) was born at normal mendelian ratios.
source: Offspring with the Srf fl/fl; Atoh1Cre genotype (hereafter referred to as Srf cKO) was born at normal mendelian ratios, but displayed reduced body weight and a relatively weak appearance, and mostly died in the third postnatal week (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B), potentially due to Atoh1-Cre recombinase activity in the intestine and the brain (Shroyer et al., 2007; Yang et al., 2010; Alberti et al., 2005).
evidence: Observation from breeding experiments

claim: Srf cKO mice displayed reduced body weight and a relatively weak appearance, and mostly died in the third postnatal week.
source: Offspring with the Srf fl/fl; Atoh1Cre genotype (hereafter referred to as Srf cKO) was born at normal mendelian ratios, but displayed reduced body weight and a relatively weak appearance, and mostly died in the third postnatal week (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B), potentially due to Atoh1-Cre recombinase activity in the intestine and the brain (Shroyer et al., 2007; Yang et al., 2010; Alberti et al., 2005).
evidence: Observed phenotype documented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B

claim: The early death of Srf cKO mice is potentially due to Atoh1-Cre recombinase activity in the intestine and the brain.
source: Offspring with the Srf fl/fl; Atoh1Cre genotype (hereafter referred to as Srf cKO) was born at normal mendelian ratios, but displayed reduced body weight and a relatively weak appearance, and mostly died in the third postnatal week (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B), potentially due to Atoh1-Cre recombinase activity in the intestine and the brain (Shroyer et al., 2007; Yang et al., 2010; Alberti et al., 2005).
evidence: Inference based on known Atoh1-Cre activity patterns supported by citations

claim: Gross morphology of the inner ear was not significantly affected in Srf cKO mice.
source: However, gross morphology of the inner ear was not significantly affected (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Observation documented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C

claim: SRF protein expression became undetectable at P0 in hair cells but not in supporting cells in Srf cKO mice.
source: To validate hair cell-specific knockout of Srf, we confirmed that SRF protein expression became undetectable at P0 in hair cells but not in supporting cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D

claim: Srf mRNA level in hair cells isolated from Srf cKO pups was significantly reduced compared to control hair cells.
source: We further confirmed that Srf mRNA level in hair cells isolated from Srf cKO pups was significantly reduced compared to control hair cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E

claim: The cuticular plate of inner hair cells (IHCs) and outer hair cells (OHCs) from Srf cKO mice displayed a significant reduction in the amount of F-actin as indicated by phalloidin staining.
source: Upon closer inspection, we found that the cuticular plate of inner hair cells (IHCs) and outer hair cells (OHCs) from Srf cKO mice displayed a significant reduction in the amount of F-actin as indicated by phalloidin staining (Figure 1A, B).
evidence: Phalloidin staining data shown in Figure 1A, B

claim: LMO7 displayed a more punctate distribution in the cuticular plate of Srf cKO mice.
source: LMO7, an actin-binding protein important for F-actin network organization (Du et al., 2019), displayed a more punctate distribution in the cuticular plate (Figure 1C).
evidence: Immunostaining data shown in Figure 1C

claim: LMO7 is an actin-binding protein important for F-actin network organization.
source: LMO7, an actin-binding protein important for F-actin network organization (Du et al., 2019), displayed a more punctate distribution in the cuticular plate (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by citation to Du et al., 2019

claim: The length of TRIOBP-positive rootlets was significantly reduced in Srf cKO mice.
source: Although the spatial organization of the rootlets appeared normal, the length of TRIOBP-positive rootlets was significantly reduced in Srf cKO mice, along with the intensity of TRIOBP staining (Figure 1D, E).
evidence: Immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 1D, E

claim: The intensity of TRIOBP staining was reduced in Srf cKO mice.
source: Although the spatial organization of the rootlets appeared normal, the length of TRIOBP-positive rootlets was significantly reduced in Srf cKO mice, along with the intensity of TRIOBP staining (Figure 1D, E).
evidence: Immunostaining data shown in Figure 1D, E

claim: TRIOBP is an actin-bundling protein that is an essential component of the rootlets.
source: The rootlets are wrapped with TRIOBP, an actin-bundling protein that is an essential component of the rootlets (Kitajiri et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kitajiri et al., 2010

claim: The deficit in the integrity of the cuticular plate F-actin mesh accompanied by shortened rootlets also appeared in Lmo7-deficient mice.
source: Interestingly, the deficit in the integrity of the cuticular plate F-actin mesh accompanied by shortened rootlets also appeared in Lmo7-deficient mice as described in a previous study (Du et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Du et al., 2019

claim: F-actin network in the cuticular plate is critical for the proper formation of the rootlets.
source: This similarity suggests that F-actin network in the cuticular plate is critical for the proper formation of the rootlets, although the causal connection between them remains unknown.
evidence: Inference based on similarity of phenotypes between Srf cKO and Lmo7-deficient mice

claim: The cuticular plate volume was reduced in Srf cKO mice.
source: The results of the cuticular plate volume (CP volume) (Figure 1F, G) were consistent with the relative F-actin fluorescence intensity change of the cuticular plate (Figure 1A, B).
evidence: 3D reconstruction and quantification data shown in Figure 1F, G

claim: The cuticular plates in Srf cKO mice were markedly thinner compared to control in IHCs at P10.
source: The TEM results demonstrated that the cuticular plates in Srf cKO mice were markedly thinner compared to control in IHCs at P10 (Figure 1H).
evidence: TEM data shown in Figure 1H

claim: Vesicle-like structures were often seen in the cuticular plate of Srf cKO OHCs at P10.
source: Although TEM images did not indicate an obvious reduction in the thickness of F-actin meshwork in P10 Srf cKO OHCs, the vesicle-like structures were often seen in the cuticular plate of the mutants (Figure 1I).
evidence: TEM data shown in Figure 1I

claim: The significant reduction of F-actin intensity in Srf cKO OHCs may partially be caused by the vesicle-like structures occupation in the cuticular plate.
source: The significant reduction of F-actin intensity indicating by phalloidin staining in Srf cKO OHCs (Figure 1B) may partially be caused by the vesicle-like structures occupation in the cuticular plate.
evidence: Inference based on TEM and phalloidin staining observations

claim: The deformation of the overlying plasma membrane above the cuticular plate of OHCs were revealed by scanning electron microscopy in Srf cKO mutants.
source: The deformation of the overlying plasma membrane above the cuticular plate of OHCs were also revealed by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) in mutants (Figure 2F, as indicated by arrows).
evidence: SEM data shown in Figure 2F

claim: At P5, the staircase-like architecture of Srf cKO hair bundles developed well.
source: At P5, the staircase-like architecture of Srf cKO hair bundles developed well, but the length of row 1 (the longest row) IHC stereocilia was slightly reduced, which worsened by P10 (Figure 2A, B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Phalloidin staining data shown in Figure 2A, B

claim: The length of row 1 IHC stereocilia was slightly reduced at P5 in Srf cKO mice, which worsened by P10.
source: At P5, the staircase-like architecture of Srf cKO hair bundles developed well, but the length of row 1 (the longest row) IHC stereocilia was slightly reduced, which worsened by P10 (Figure 2A, B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Phalloidin staining and quantification data shown in Figure 2A, B

claim: The length of row 1 IHC stereocilia was significantly reduced in Srf cKO mutants at P10.
source: SEM further revealed that the length of row 1 IHC, the length of row 1 OHC, and the width of row 1 IHC stereocilia were significantly reduced in mutants at P10, but no statistical difference was found for the width of row 1 OHC stereocilia yet (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: SEM data and quantification shown in Figure 2C–E

claim: The length of row 1 OHC stereocilia was significantly reduced in Srf cKO mutants at P10.
source: SEM further revealed that the length of row 1 IHC, the length of row 1 OHC, and the width of row 1 IHC stereocilia were significantly reduced in mutants at P10, but no statistical difference was found for the width of row 1 OHC stereocilia yet (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: SEM data and quantification shown in Figure 2C–E

claim: The width of row 1 IHC stereocilia was significantly reduced in Srf cKO mutants at P10.
source: SEM further revealed that the length of row 1 IHC, the length of row 1 OHC, and the width of row 1 IHC stereocilia were significantly reduced in mutants at P10, but no statistical difference was found for the width of row 1 OHC stereocilia yet (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: SEM data and quantification shown in Figure 2C–E

claim: No statistical difference was found for the width of row 1 OHC stereocilia at P10 in Srf cKO mutants.
source: SEM further revealed that the length of row 1 IHC, the length of row 1 OHC, and the width of row 1 IHC stereocilia were significantly reduced in mutants at P10, but no statistical difference was found for the width of row 1 OHC stereocilia yet (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: SEM data and quantification shown in Figure 2C–E

claim: The length and width of row 1 IHC stereocilia were obviously reduced in Srf cKO mutants at P15 and P24.
source: Immunocytochemistry showed that the length and width of row 1 IHC stereocilia were obviously reduced in mutants at P15 and P24, as well as the width of stereocilia in utricles (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B

claim: The width of stereocilia in utricles was reduced in Srf cKO mutants.
source: Immunocytochemistry showed that the length and width of row 1 IHC stereocilia were obviously reduced in mutants at P15 and P24, as well as the width of stereocilia in utricles (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B

claim: The width of rows 1 and 2 IHC stereocilia was drastically reduced by 40% in Srf cKO at P15.
source: Statistical analysis of SEM images confirmed that the width of rows 1 and 2 IHC stereocilia was drastically reduced by 40% in Srf cKO at P15 (Figure 2G, H).
evidence: SEM data and quantification shown in Figure 2G, H

claim: Numerous microvilli still persisted in Srf cKO IHCs at P15, indicating a lack of mature hair bundle characteristics.
source: At P15, numerous microvilli still persisted in Srf cKO IHCs, indicating a lack of mature hair bundle characteristics, but this was not the case for Srf cKO OHCs (Figure 2F, G).
evidence: SEM data shown in Figure 2F, G

claim: Microvilli did not persist in Srf cKO OHCs at P15.
source: At P15, numerous microvilli still persisted in Srf cKO IHCs, indicating a lack of mature hair bundle characteristics, but this was not the case for Srf cKO OHCs (Figure 2F, G).
evidence: SEM data shown in Figure 2F, G

claim: The kinocilium degenerates in mouse cochlear hair cells from base to apex at P8 and disappears completely around P12.
source: The kinocilium, a microtubule-based cilium that is essential for the polarity of the developing hair bundle, degenerates in mouse cochlear hair cells from base to apex at P8 and disappears completely around P12 (Haag et al., 2018; Leibovici et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citations to Haag et al., 2018 and Leibovici et al., 2005

claim: More kinocilia remained in Srf cKO IHCs compared to the controls at P10.
source: Confocal microscopy images showed that more kinocilia remained in Srf cKO IHCs compared to the controls at P10 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, D).
evidence: Confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, D

claim: SRF is required for the development as well as the maintenance of the F-actin-enriched hair bundle and the cuticular plate.
source: We conclude that SRF is required for the development as well as the maintenance of the F-actin-enriched hair bundle and the cuticular plate.
evidence: Conclusion based on multiple observations of Srf cKO phenotypes

claim: ESPN1 is an isoform of ESPN, which is an actin-binding and bundling protein required for the elongation of hair cell stereocilia.
source: ESPN1, an isoform of ESPN, which is an actin-binding and bundling protein, is required for the elongation of hair cell stereocilia (Ebrahim et al., 2016; Rzadzinska et al., 2005; Salles et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Ebrahim et al., 2016; Rzadzinska et al., 2005; Salles et al., 2009

claim: EPS8 and GNAI3 are components of the row 1 complex essential for controlling the elongation of the tallest row of stereocilia during hair bundle morphological development.
source: Similarly, EPS8 and GNAI3, which are components of the row 1 complex, are essential for controlling the elongation of the tallest row of stereocilia during hair bundle morphological development (Tarchini et al., 2016; Zampini et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Tarchini et al., 2016 and Zampini et al., 2011

claim: The relative row 1 tip fluorescence signal intensity for ESPN1 and EPS8 dramatically decreased starting at P4 in Srf cKO IHCs.
source: The dramatic decreases of the relative row 1 tip fluorescence signal intensity for ESPN1 and EPS8, but not GNAI3, started since P4 in Srf cKO IHCs.
evidence: Immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 3A–F

claim: The decrease of GNAI3 in Srf cKO IHCs was observed at P10.
source: The decrease of GNAI3 in Srf cKO IHCs was observed soon after at P10 (Figure 3A–F).
evidence: Immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 3A–F

claim: Irregular labeling in different stereocilia of the same row were observed for ESPN1, EPS8, and GNAI3 in Srf cKO mice.
source: In addition to the reduced row 1 tip localization of ESPN1, EPS8, and GNAI3, the irregular labeling in different stereocilia of the same row were also observed in these tested proteins in Srf cKO mice (Figure 3G–I).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3G–I

claim: The row 2 tip signals of ESPN1, EPS8, and GNAI3 were partially maintained in Srf cKO IHCs compared to controls at P10.
source: Meanwhile, the row 2 tip signals of ESPN1, EPS8, and GNAI3 were partially maintained in Srf cKO IHCs compared to controls, although the expression of EPS8 and GNAI3 were abundant in row 1 tip and absent in row 2 tip in controls at P10 (Figure 3J–L).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3J–L

claim: The expression of EPS8 and GNAI3 were abundant in row 1 tip and absent in row 2 tip in controls at P10.
source: Meanwhile, the row 2 tip signals of ESPN1, EPS8, and GNAI3 were partially maintained in Srf cKO IHCs compared to controls, although the expression of EPS8 and GNAI3 were abundant in row 1 tip and absent in row 2 tip in controls at P10 (Figure 3J–L).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3J–L

claim: FSCN2 is an abundantly expressed actin-crosslinking protein in stereocilia.
source: We also quantified the relative fluorescence signals of FSCN2, an abundantly expressed actin-crosslinking protein in stereocilia (Perrin et al., 2013), within the stereocilia shaft.
evidence: Supported by citation to Perrin et al., 2013

claim: The fluorescence levels of FSCN2 were significantly reduced by 20% in Srf cKO IHCs at P10.
source: The fluorescence levels were significantly reduced by 20% in Srf cKO IHCs at P10 (Figure 3M, N).
evidence: Immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 3M, N

claim: Srf deficiency in hair cells compromises the integrity of F-actin mesh in the cuticular plate and reduces the dimensions of stereocilia.
source: In summary, Srf deficiency in hair cells compromises the integrity of F-actin mesh in the cuticular plate and reduces the dimensions of stereocilia.
evidence: Summary conclusion based on multiple experimental observations

claim: Mrtfa and Mrtfb have low levels of transcripts during inner ear development.
source: Previous studies have identified Mrtfa and Mrtfb, the members of MRTF family, as having low levels of transcripts during inner ear development (Cai et al., 2015; Elkon et al., 2015; Scheffer et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Cai et al., 2015; Elkon et al., 2015; Scheffer et al., 2015

claim: Mrtfa and Mrtfb are ubiquitously expressed in E16 cochlea, including in hair cells.
source: In the present study, we employed RNAscope staining to confirm the ubiquitous expression of Mrtfa and Mrtfb in E16 cochlea, including in hair cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: RNAscope staining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A

claim: Mrtfa cKO and Mrtfb cKO mice were viable and fertile with no overt phenotype.
source: Crossing these mice to Atoh1-Cre line resulted in the production of Mrtfa cKO and Mrtfb cKO mice, which were viable and fertile with no overt phenotype.
evidence: Observation from breeding experiments

claim: Mrtfa mRNA and protein levels were partially reduced in hair cells of Mrtfa cKO mice.
source: Mrtfa mRNA and protein levels, as well as MRTFB protein immunoreactivity, were partially reduced in hair cells of respective knockout mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, D and Figure 4—figure supplement 2C, D).
evidence: RNAscope and immunostaining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, D

claim: MRTFB protein immunoreactivity was partially reduced in hair cells of Mrtfb cKO mice.
source: Mrtfa mRNA and protein levels, as well as MRTFB protein immunoreactivity, were partially reduced in hair cells of respective knockout mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, D and Figure 4—figure supplement 2C, D).
evidence: Immunostaining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C, D

claim: No significant changes were observed in the intensity of F-actin in the cuticular plate and the length of row 1 IHC stereocilia in Mrtfa mutants at P26.
source: We measured the intensity of F-actin in the cuticular plate and the length of row 1 IHC stereocilia in Mrtfa mutants and observed no significant changes compared to controls at P26 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E–G).
evidence: Phalloidin staining and quantification data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E–G

claim: Mrtfa cKO mice showed normal hearing at P26.
source: Additionally, auditory brainstem responses (ABRs) measurements and distortion product otoacoustic emissions (DPOAEs) recordings indicated normal hearing of Mrtfa cKO mice at P26 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: ABR and DPOAE data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1H

claim: A notable decrease in F-actin intensity was observed in the cuticular plate of Mrtfb cKO OHCs.
source: Specifically, a notable decrease in F-actin intensity was observed in the cuticular plate of Mrtfb cKO OHCs, with a trend toward reduced F-actin intensity noted in the cuticular plate of Mrtfb cKO IHCs (Figure 4A, B).
evidence: Phalloidin staining and quantification data shown in Figure 4A, B

claim: A trend toward reduced F-actin intensity was noted in the cuticular plate of Mrtfb cKO IHCs.
source: Specifically, a notable decrease in F-actin intensity was observed in the cuticular plate of Mrtfb cKO OHCs, with a trend toward reduced F-actin intensity noted in the cuticular plate of Mrtfb cKO IHCs (Figure 4A, B).
evidence: Phalloidin staining and quantification data shown in Figure 4A, B

claim: The length of TRIOBP-positive rootlets was reduced in Mrtfb cKO mutants.
source: Additionally, the length of TRIOBP-positive rootlets was reduced in the mutants, despite no observed changes in TRIOBP staining intensity (Figure 4C, D).
evidence: Immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 4C, D

claim: No observed changes in TRIOBP staining intensity were found in Mrtfb cKO mutants.
source: Additionally, the length of TRIOBP-positive rootlets was reduced in the mutants, despite no observed changes in TRIOBP staining intensity (Figure 4C, D).
evidence: Immunostaining data shown in Figure 4C, D

claim: The cuticular plates in Mrtfb cKO mice were markedly thinner compared to control in OHCs at P10.
source: Using TEM analysis, the results demonstrated that the cuticular plates in Mrtfb cKO mice were markedly thinner compared to control in OHCs at P10.
evidence: TEM data shown in Figure 4G, H

claim: Vesicle-like structures occupation in the cuticular plate were observed in Mrtfb cKO mutants.
source: The vesicle-like structures occupation in the cuticular plate were also observed in the mutants.
evidence: TEM data shown in Figure 4G, H

claim: The reduction of the cuticular plate thickness in Mrtfb cKO mice was more pronounced at P26.
source: The reduction of the cuticular plate thickness in Mrtfb cKO mice was more pronounced at P26.
evidence: TEM data shown in Figure 4G, H

claim: A decrease of the cuticular plate thickness in Mrtfb cKO IHCs was observed at P26.
source: For IHCs, a decrease of the cuticular plate thickness in Mrtfb cKO was observed until P26 (Figure 4G, H).
evidence: TEM data shown in Figure 4G, H

claim: At P5, no difference in row 1 IHC stereocilia length was observed between the control and Mrtfb cKO mice.
source: At P5, no difference in row 1 IHC stereocilia length was observed between the control and Mrtfb cKO mice.
evidence: Immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 5A, B

claim: The length of row 1 IHC stereocilia was significantly reduced at P10 and P26 in Mrtfb cKO mice.
source: However, the length of row 1 IHC stereocilia was significantly reduced at P10 and P26 (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: Immunocytochemistry and quantification data shown in Figure 5A, B

claim: The staircase-like architecture of Mrtfb cKO OHC hair bundles formed adequately at P10, but progressively degenerated throughout development.
source: While the staircase-like architecture of Mrtfb cKO OHC hair bundles formed adequately at P10, they progressively degenerated throughout development (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Phalloidin staining data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A

claim: A slight reduction in stereocilia width was observed in OHCs of Mrtfb cKO mutants at P10, with the length of stereocilia remaining intact.
source: Specifically, a slight reduction in stereocilia width was observed in OHCs, with the length of stereocilia remaining intact in mutants at P10 (Figure 5C, E).
evidence: SEM data and quantification shown in Figure 5C, E

claim: By P42, the stereocilia of OHCs had severely degenerated in Mrtfb cKO mice.
source: However, by P42, the stereocilia of OHCs had severely degenerated (Figure 5F).
evidence: SEM data shown in Figure 5F

claim: Both the length and width of row 1 stereocilia showed significant decreases in Mrtfb mutant IHCs at P10 and P42.
source: For IHCs, both the length and width of row 1 stereocilia showed significant decreases in Mrtfb mutants at P10 (Figure 5D, E) and P42 (Figure 5G, H).
evidence: SEM data and quantification shown in Figure 5D, E, G, H

claim: Defects in the dimensions of stereocilia of utricle hair cells were observed in Mrtfb cKO mice.
source: Notably, defects in the dimensions of stereocilia of utricle hair cells were also observed in Mrtfb cKO mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Phalloidin staining data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B

claim: An obvious decrease in the relative row 1 tip fluorescence signal intensity for ESPN1 was initially observed at P10 in Mrtfb cKO mutants.
source: As shown in Figure 6, an obvious decrease in the relative row 1 tip fluorescence signal intensity for ESPN1 was initially observed at P10 in the mutants.
evidence: Immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 6A–F

claim: The obvious reduction of relative row 1 tip fluorescence signal intensity of EPS8 and GNAI3 appeared around P15 in Mrtfb cKO.
source: Compared to ESPN1, the obvious reduction of relative row 1 tip fluorescence signal intensity of EPS8 and GNAI3 appeared much later in Mrtfb cKO, around P15 (Figure 6A–F).
evidence: Immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 6A–F

claim: The irregular labeling of ESPN1 and GNAI3 in different stereocilia of the same row were occasionally observed in Mrtfb cKO mice.
source: The irregular labeling of ESPN1 and GNAI3 in different stereocilia of the same row were occasionally observed in Mrtfb cKO mice (Figure 6G–I).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6G–I

claim: The distribution of ESPN1, EPS8, and GNAI3 between rows 1 and 2 stereocilia were not affected in Mrtfb cKO mice at P10.
source: The distribution of these proteins between rows 1 and 2 stereocilia were not affected in Mrtfb cKO mice at P10 (Figure 6J–L).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6J–L

claim: The fluorescence signals of FSCN2 within the stereocilia shaft were dramatically reduced by 40% in Mrtfb cKO IHCs.
source: Additionally, The fluorescence signals of FSCN2 within the stereocilia shaft were dramatically reduced by 40% in Mrtfb cKO IHCs (Figure 6M, N).
evidence: Immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 6M, N

claim: At P26, the ABR thresholds of Mrtfb cKO mice were significantly elevated, with more pronounced effects at mid- to high frequencies ranging from 11 to 32 kHz.
source: At P26, the ABR thresholds of Mrtfb cKO mice were significantly elevated, with more pronounced effects at mid- to high frequencies ranging from 11 to 32 kHz.
evidence: ABR data shown in Figure 7A

claim: By P40, Mrtfb cKO mice developed profound hearing loss at all frequencies tested, with ABR thresholds that were 40–60 dB higher than those of the control group.
source: By P40, Mrtfb cKO mice developed profound hearing loss at all frequencies tested, with ABR thresholds that were 40–60 dB higher than those of the control group (Figure 7A).
evidence: ABR data shown in Figure 7A

claim: DPOAE thresholds of Mrtfb cKO mice were markedly elevated over the 11–32 kHz frequency range.
source: Consistent with ABRs measurements, DPOAE thresholds of Mrtfb cKO mice were markedly elevated over the 11–32 kHz frequency range.
evidence: DPOAE data shown in Figure 7B

claim: From P40 onward, the DPOAE thresholds increased progressively for all frequencies in Mrtfb cKO mice.
source: From P40 onward, the DPOAE thresholds increased progressively for all frequencies (Figure 7B).
evidence: DPOAE data shown in Figure 7B

claim: The amplitude of ABR wave 1 was reduced at 80–90 dB in Mrtfb cKO mice compared to normal hearing control mice.
source: In comparison to normal hearing control mice, the amplitude of ABR wave 1 was reduced at 80–90 dB, and the latency of ABR wave 1 was significantly prolonged (Figure 7C).
evidence: ABR wave 1 analysis shown in Figure 7C

claim: The latency of ABR wave 1 was significantly prolonged in Mrtfb cKO mice compared to normal hearing control mice.
source: In comparison to normal hearing control mice, the amplitude of ABR wave 1 was reduced at 80–90 dB, and the latency of ABR wave 1 was significantly prolonged (Figure 7C).
evidence: ABR wave 1 analysis shown in Figure 7C

claim: The expression level and localization of Prestin were normal in Mrtfb mutants.
source: Our results showed that the expression level and localization of Prestin were normal in Mrtfb mutants (Figure 7D).
evidence: Immunostaining data shown in Figure 7D

claim: No significant differences were found in nonlinear capacitance, total number of Prestin (Qmax), cell sizes (Clin), charge density (Qsp), and voltage sensitivity (Vh) between Mrtfb cKO and control mice at P18.
source: We quantified the nonlinear capacitance, total number of Prestin (Qmax), cell sizes (Clin), charge density (Qsp), and voltage sensitivity (Vh), and found no significant differences between Mrtfb cKO and control mice (Figure 7E–I).
evidence: Whole-cell patch-clamp recording data shown in Figure 7E–I

claim: Mrtfb is not required for the development of OHC electromotility during early postnatal stages.
source: These findings suggest that Mrtfb is not required for the development of OHC electromotility during early postnatal stages.
evidence: Inference based on electromotility measurements

claim: The number of CtBP2-positive synapses in Mrtfb mutants was comparable to controls.
source: The number of CtBP2-positive synapses in Mrtfb mutants was comparable to controls, and normal co-localization of CtBP2 and Cav1.3, as well as CtBP2 and GluR2, was observed (Figure 7J–L).
evidence: Immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 7J–L

claim: Normal co-localization of CtBP2 and Cav1.3, as well as CtBP2 and GluR2, was observed in Mrtfb mutants.
source: The number of CtBP2-positive synapses in Mrtfb mutants was comparable to controls, and normal co-localization of CtBP2 and Cav1.3, as well as CtBP2 and GluR2, was observed (Figure 7J–L).
evidence: Immunostaining data shown in Figure 7J–L

claim: Hair cell numbers in Mrtfb cKO mice were nearly intact at P26 and P42, except for a reduction in OHC numbers at the base of Mrtfb cKO cochleae at P42.
source: Our results indicated that hair cell numbers in Mrtfb cKO mice were nearly intact, except for a reduction in OHC numbers at the base of Mrtfb cKO cochleae at P42 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Hair cell counting data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, B

claim: The early-onset hearing loss observed in Mrtfb mutants is not primarily caused by hair cell loss.
source: This suggests that the early-onset hearing loss observed in Mrtfb mutants is not primarily caused by hair cell loss.
evidence: Inference based on hair cell counting data

claim: 110 up-regulated and 79 down-regulated DEGs were identified in Srf cKO hair cells.
source: We performed differential gene expression analysis (padj < 0.05 and |log2(fold change)| > 1) (Figure 8B), and identified 110 up-regulated and 79 down-regulated DEGs in Srf cKO hair cells (the down-regulated genes hereinafter referred to as Srf targets), and 15 up-regulated and 105 down-regulated DEGs in Mrtfb cKO hair cells (the down-regulated genes hereinafter referred to as Mrtfb targets).
